title: SE Journals in 2036: Looking Back at the Future We Need to Have

edges.target: Price's Square Root Law (de Solla Price)
edges.ref: [7] Derek J. de Solla Price. 1963. Little Science, Big Science. Columbia University Press.
edges.evidence: This number is larger than what might be predicted by Price's law [7] since sqrt(18,500) = 136 < 500. Nevertheless, it is still consistent with "most of the highly recognized work comes from a very small core".

edges.ref: [1] Corinna Cortes and Neil D. Lawrence. 2021. Inconsistency in Conference Peer Review: Revisiting the 2014 NeurIPS Experiment. arXiv:2109.09774
edges.evidence: Experiments at AI conferences [1] reveal that independent review teams disagree on 50% of accepted papers. This suggests that peer review and "getting published" are stochastic

edges.ref: [10] Abhik Roychoudhury. 2026. A Year in TOSEM: New Research Award, Agentic AI Special Issue and Much More. ACM TOSEM 35, 1 (2026).
edges.evidence: A 2025 editorial in TOSEM [10] underscored the large volume of submissions. In terms of concrete numbers, there were around 2000 submissions to TOSEM in 2025 ... handled within 67 days on average

edges.ref: [9] Lambros Roumbanis. 2019. Peer Review or Lottery? ... Science, Technology, & Human Values 44, 6 (2019), 994-1019.
edges.evidence: it was natural to take the advice of Roumbanis [9] and restructure journal reviewing as a lottery process.

edges.ref: [4] Arjun K Manrai, David Ouyang, Joseph W Hogan, and Isaac S Kohane. 2025. Accelerating science with Human+ AI review. AIe2501175.
edges.evidence: we adopted the "Human+AI" philosophy proposed by Manrai et al. [4]. They argued that AI should never be an arbiter of scientific merit

edges.target: ACM SIGSOFT Empirical Standards (Ralph et al.)
edges.ref: [8] Paul Ralph et al. 2021. Empirical Standards for Software Engineering Research. arXiv:2010.03525
edges.evidence: These documents mention around 135 review items. After asking Gemini to abstract those items, we found that there are variants of 12 core features.
